answer: The mesa multiplier is published, charged in ocean, and gale lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 977 identities would post 3281 proofs and burn roughly 44 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
